# MILD TO MODERATE SINUSITIS

Community-acquired bacterial sinusitis is most often due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae or Moraxella catarrhalis. Streptococci, Staphylococcus aureus and anaerobes are isolated less frequently.

---

References:

- Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h ($) [R] for 5 days
- Non-VA order for above
- Alternatives:
- [Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
- Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h ($) [R] for 5 days
- Non-VA order for above

< OR >

- Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h ($) [DI] for 5 days
- Non-VA order for above

## Treatment Failure

If symptoms worsen despite 72 hours or fail to improve after 3-5 days of initial empirical antimicrobial therapy, broaden coverage, switch to different antimicrobial class and treat 7-10 days. If symptoms continue to worsen or there is no improvement after 3-5 more days of treatment, obtain CT to investigate non-infectious or suppurative causes. ENT consultation is recommended. If sinuses are aspirated, specimens should be cultured.
Levofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h ($) [R,DI] for 7 days
Non-VA order for above

Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Treatment for first 10 days of illness

Treat with decongestants, analgesics, and nasal saline spray.

### Treatment of cases that have not improved in 10 days despite treatment with decongestants, analgesics, and nasal saline.

Preferred:

Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h ($) [R] for 5 days
Alternatives:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
